lines.text: Do you know how a lost AirTag finds its way home, with no GPS and no SIM?
You leave your bag on a train. Inside, a tiny tag keeps whispering one thing. I'm here.
It's a Bluetooth beacon. A short ping every couple of seconds, with a code that keeps changing.
Any iPhone passing by quietly adds its own location, locks it with the tag's key, and sends it up.
Only your phone can open it. Apple can't read where your bag is, and neither can the stranger who walked past.
You open the app, and a dot pops up on the map. Your bag, three stops down the line.
Orbi Transfer works with the people around you too. Files pop up on nearby screens, locked on the sender's phone, and only the right code opens them.
